builds.name: Half Health Hell
builds.desc:
This Build abuses the Brash Assault 3 Desperation 3 Combo to turn Gratia+ into a high Mt Brave Weapon that can also nullify ranged buffs or guarantee a quad with Brave Bow+ .
Weapon: Gratia+ nullify buff effect is especially useful in the arena to counter the Blade Tome users and Horse Emblem Reinhardt but Brave Bow+ is more useful in general and plays better into L!Roy's stats.
Assist: Reposition is my preferred movement assist for Horse Emblem but Ardent Sacrifice is useful to get L!Roy to the HP≤50% threshold to utilize this build. L!Roy comes with Reciprocal Aid and it can play the same role as Ardent Sacrifice would if you want a lower cost alternative.
Special: Draconic Aura is a reliable way to add that extra punch if needed but if you prefer higher damage to lower cool down the Dragon Fang works too. Both play well into L!Roy's high Atk stat that only gets higher when given proper buffs in Horse Emblem and with Death Blow 3.
Horse Emblem is optimal to give L!Roy maximum Atk buffs but pairing him with dancers that have Wings of Mercy 3 would also be very effective once he gets below half health.
With Desperation 3 and the Brash Assault 3 seal, L!Roy can double with Gratia+ and quad with Brave Bow+ without being counter attacked. This is the main part of the build but it is risky due to L!Roy having to have at most half health but it can unleash hell upon your enemies. High Risk, High Reward.

builds.name: Roy, Brave Lover
builds.desc:
V!Roy's stats are absolutely perfect for a brave set; low speed, good attack, and pretty good other stats as well.
Weapon: Brave Bow+ is by a very large margin V!Roy's best weapon due to his low speed. Brave Bow+ will allow him to initiate twice on opponents, dealing large amounts of damage to the opponent.
Assist: Reposition, as with most cavalry units, works very well on V!Roy, allowing him to move other units in and out of combat.
Special: Dragon Fang works very well as a special, boosting his already good attack even higher. Moonbow will also work well as a special, of course, due to its low cooldown time.
A Passive: Death Blow 3 is the absolute best A passive for this build, as it allows V!Roy to do a lot more damage going out.
B Passive: Swordbreaker 3 and Lancebreaker 3 are two very good B passives for V!Roy, as they help him greatly with matchups against common sword and lance users. Use whichever one you think would be better on your team.
C Passive: As with most units, the C passive is open to whatever your team needs most. On a cavalry team, Hone Cavalry works very well.
Sacred Seal: In order to boost his already-good attack (and to make up for the 7mt of Brave Bow+), Attack +3 is recommended as V!Roy's seal.

builds.name: Enemy Phase Boy
builds.desc:
For a kind of different more interesting type of build I wanted to make use of V!Roy's fairly good defense and Resistance. Sadly this can be a bit muddled by V!Roy's subpar HP but with Summoner support that can be mildly fixed
Weapon - Guard Bow+ with a Defense refine is used to even out V!Roy's defense stat as well as give him the Distant Def 3 effect to make him better against ranged weapon users.
Assist - Reposition / Draw Back is used as with most other teams to make movement much easier.
Special - Iceberg / Bonfire can be used interchangeably with V!Roy since he will be equal in each stat and both provide great consistent damage.
A Passive - Close Counter is used to allow roy to counter attack up close on the enemy phase which can be really useful for him to tank hits as well as have a chance to counter against melee fliers.
B Passive - Quick Riposte 4 is chosen as a must have on most enemy phase units and V!Roy is no exception.
C Passive - Hone Cavalry / Fortify Cavalry can be used interchangeably as well for Horse Emblem teams just depending on which is preferable to you.
S Passive - Close Def 3 is chosen to boost V!Roy's Defence and resistance up close and support his close counter.
Hope this build works out well for you, Good Luck Summoners!

builds.name: No Blade Tomes Allowed!
builds.desc:
Hey guys, Trinitronity is here. I'm a giant Roy fan, so of course I checked for possible builds for him, but I didn't saw any for the IVs of my Roy...or any that use his original weapon for that matter. So I decided to fix that by making a build to counter blade tome users, with a little help from the FEH Discord server.
Weapon: Gratia+ with a Res define is the main source of the anti-Blade nature of this build. The weapon itself negates all buffs (including the Blade tomes' additional buffs) while also boosting Roy's resistance even more, just to shield him from tome attacks even better.
Assist: Reposition and Draw Back are very common movement assist skills and also really useful. While Reposition is more useful in Horse Emblem teams, Draw Back is still a good alternative.
Special: Draconic Aura works very well as a special, boosting his already good attack by a good margin. Even though the boost in attack is not as high as with Dragon Fang, but having a lower cooldown definitely helps. Iceberg will also work well as a special, of course, due to LA!Roy's high Res stats, though you probably want him to be buffed by Fortifies first.
A Passive: Fury 3 is a really good A passive for both Player Phase and Enemy Phase, since it boosts both his attack and his resistance at the cost of recoil damage. It was originally going to be Distant Defense 3, but due to how hard that skill is to come by, I had to make Distant Defense 3 a seal instead.
B Passive: G Tomebreaker 3 and R Tomebreaker 3 are two very good B passives an anti-Blade LA!Roy, as they help him greatly with matchups against common blade tome users like Cecilia, Nino and other. Use whichever one you think would be better on your team. I would have included Quick Riposte 3 as an alternative as well, but I wont as long as that skill is still locked to 5-Star units.
C Passive: As with most units, the C passive is open to whatever your team needs most. On a cavalry team, Hone Cavalry works very well.
S Passive - Distant Def 3 and Deflect Magic 3 are chosen to boost LA!Roy's resistance, shielding him from Blade tome users even more.

builds.name: Look at me, I'm Brave Lyn
builds.desc:
When I first saw Valentines Roy was a cavalry bow, I immediately joked about him being diet Lyn. This set comes from having thought further on it, and taking that joke to a bit of an extreme by recreating Lyn's default kit as closely as possible with Roy.
First of all, we stick with the default weapon, because it actually imitates Brave Lyn's bow pretty nicely. You trade some base damage for ignoring buffs from everyone, not just mages. With a refinement, you also trade one speed for two HP, which isn't too bad.
Draconic Aura is the same as what Lyn regularly has, and also will work perfectly fine with Roy, thanks to his high base Attack. If you wanted to, you could use Iceberg as well.
Swift Sparrow 2 is the same thing as what Lyn has, but due to how we're replicating Lyn, it also plays a role in assisting Roy with Windsweep's effect. If you don't have a Swift Sparrow to spare, or are more concerned about guaranteeing Windsweep activates, Darting Blow 3 is a decent alternative that isn't too hard to get.
Windsweep 3 is our way of imitating Sacae's Blessing - while Roy's speed is low enough that he isn't too bothered losing a second hit, it does mean we really have to focus on his speed to get it to activate reliably. However, with a +Spd nature, Speed refinement, Swift Sparrow, and Phantom Spd 3, we can get his Speed effectively up to 38 - this just about guarantees that Windsweep will activate on everyone who you'd be worried about retaliating against you. And we're not even considering Cavalry buffs.
The last slot is effectively free, but since we have a theme, I've gone with what you'd probably see on a Brave Lyn - Atk Smoke 3 or Hone Cavalry. However, you can use whatever is most useful for you here.
Now, unfortunately, this build has a lot of investment to even get close to what Lyn can do out of the box, but it's not all bad - Roy does actually have some upsides with this set. His combination of abilities lets him deal with enemy bows more easily, even ones who carry Bowbreaker 3, which can be helpful. Daggers are also covered, but they're not as common.
